findings.location: Paragraph beginning "While they stood before the Lord..." (third full paragraph after first scripture block)
findings.source_quote: As they stood before the Lord, waiting for Him to speak, the Spirit of the Lord came down and God gave them the words of help and hope that they were desperate for.
findings.suggested_fix: Adjust Dutch sentence order/subject to read more naturally while preserving meaning and theology. For example: replace "...en gaf God hun de woorden van hulp en hoop waar ze zo naar snakten." with "...en gaf Hij hun de woorden van hulp en hoop waar ze zo naar snakten." or "...en gaf God hen de woorden van hulp en hoop waar ze zo naar snakten." This keeps the original sense that God (and the Spirit) provided the words.
findings.translation_quote: ...terwijl ze voor de HEERE stonden en wachtten tot Hij zou spreken, kwam de Geest des HEEREN op hen neer en gaf God hun de woorden van hulp en hoop waar ze zo naar snakten.

findings.source_quote: Examples: "O LORD God of our fathers, art not thou God in heaven? and rulest not thou over all the kingdoms of the heathen? ... –verse 6."; "Be not afraid nor dismayed by reason of this great multitude... –verse 15." (multiple KJV-style quotations)
findings.suggested_fix: Translation preserves the quoted Scripture but uses archaic-form Dutch (HEERE in capitals; Gij/u alternation; older pronouns and syntax). The client requested standard contemporary Dutch. If contemporary Bible-style language is required, consider using a modern Dutch Bible register consistently (e.g. 'Heer' instead of 'HEERE', 'u' consistently rather than 'Gij'). This is a stylistic recommendation only; it must not change theological meaning or verse numbering. Example change: change 'HEERE' to 'Heer' and modernize 'Gij' → 'u' and 'uw' where appropriate, keeping all verse markers unchanged.
findings.translation_quote: Several places, e.g. "HEERE" used throughout the verse quotations: "HEERE, God onzer vaderen, zijt Gij niet God in den hemel? ... – vers 6." and similar older forms elsewhere.
